requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing when a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly is a member type. Two diagnostic sites in TypeCollector no longer index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. They now use null-safe lookups: a new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` helper and `FirstOrDefault()`. The analyzer's report callback is also wrapped so that any diagnostic whose location is not a source location in the current compilation is silently dropped. Three tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image. They check that the generator, and probably the analyzer, report no diagnostics and that a resolver is generated. README and the MsgPack004 doc gain notes about types from referenced assemblies.
story.why: REQ-2283: an IndexOutOfRangeException in TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo for metadata-only symbols made the generator drop its output entirely (CS8785) and the analyzer throw (AD0001).
touches_beyond_requirement: TypeCollector.cs line 239: every analyzer diagnostic from TypeCollector now goes through a filter. Any diagnostic with Location.None or an out-of-compilation location is silently dropped, not only those from the two fixed sites.

Line 985 changed a hard `(PropertyDeclarationSyntax)` cast to `as`. For non-property syntax (e.g. positional record parameters) the location becomes null and the diagnostic is now dropped by the filter instead of throwing.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md document new user-visible behaviour: diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are not reported in the consuming project.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the two edited sites no longer throw on metadata symbols, and that the tests reproduce the issue's record-struct scenario against a real metadata image. Medium confidence that the analyzer (not just the generator) is exercised by VerifyCS; that depends on CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier, which is not shown. Low confidence that the fix is complete: the issue names three indexing sites (735, 1009, 1101) and only two appear in the diff. The global diagnostic filter is a broader behaviour change than the bug needs.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now gets its location from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. That helper uses FirstOrDefault() and an `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast, so it returns null instead of throwing for metadata properties.

claims.text: Added usings Microsoft.CodeAnalysis and Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing support the MetadataReference, Compilation, ReferenceAssemblies and TestBehaviors types used by the new test helpers.
README and MsgPack004 docs state that referenced-assembly closed generics are supported and that member diagnostics for such types are reported only by the defining project.
The analyzer report callback is wrapped so that diagnostics are forwarded only via ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. When no callback is supplied (generator path), reportDiagnostic stays null.

claims.text: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation reports a diagnostic only if its Location is in source and its SourceTree belongs to this.compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None or metadata locations are dropped.
The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic location uses `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?`, so an unkeyed public member of a metadata type no longer throws.

RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs the VerifyCS test with no expected diagnostics. It then runs CSharpGeneratorDriver directly and asserts no warning-or-higher generator diagnostics (which would include CS8785) and that the expected resolver hint name is among the generated sources.

The referenced symbols therefore have no DeclaringSyntaxReferences, matching the issue's trigger. CreateCompilation builds the CSharpCompilation for both steps.

refusals.what: A global filter now suppresses every TypeCollector analyzer diagnostic that lacks an in-compilation source location.
refusals.why: This goes beyond fixing the IndexOutOfRangeException and changes which warnings users see, potentially hiding existing diagnostics. The UnkeyedMember test asserts this suppression, so the behaviour was chosen rather than required.

refusals.what: User-facing docs commit to a policy that diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are reported only by the defining project.
refusals.why: This documents a new user-visible analyzer behaviour that the requirement did not ask for; the owner should decide whether it is the intended contract.

findings.description: The issue lists three indexing sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff touches only the two matching 1009/1101 (offset ~25). The site near old line 735 (~710 in the new file) is not in the diff. If it also indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] on a path reachable for metadata types, the crash may remain for other shapes (e.g. different attribute/constructor configurations) that the three tests don't hit.

The filter applies to every diagnostic TypeCollector reports, not just the two fixed sites. Any existing diagnostic built with a null location (e.g. from GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation/GetParameterListLocation returning null) used to surface with Location.None. It is now silently swallowed. Users may lose real warnings, including ones about source types whose helper failed to find syntax.

The `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast returns null for positional record properties, whose syntax is a ParameterSyntax. Combined with the filter, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for an in-source positional record property is now dropped silently, where it previously threw InvalidCastException. The missing report is not tested.

Whether VerifyCS.Test (CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator>) runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer is not visible in the diff. If it only runs the generator, the AD0001 half of the bug and the new filter at line 239 are not exercised by any test.

out_of_scope.description: Global diagnostic location filter (line 239, helper 1436-1450). The crash fix only needs null-safe syntax lookups; the filter decides policy that metadata-type diagnostics are never reported in consumers.
New README section documenting referenced-assembly generic support and diagnostic ownership.
New section stating MsgPack004 does not report on members of referenced-assembly types.
